inheritance:
- name: Autosomal recessive
  description: >-
    Disease requires two damaging alleles at the same autosomal locus. In the
    consanguineous pedigrees in which most AR-NSID genes were discovered the two
    alleles are identical by descent (homozygous), so the affected haplotype
    falls inside a run of homozygosity - the property that makes autozygosity
    mapping the discovery method of choice. Compound heterozygosity is the
    corresponding mechanism in outbred families. Heterozygous carriers,
    including the obligate-carrier parents, are unaffected. Recurrence risk for
    full siblings is 25%, an order of magnitude higher than for the sporadic de
    novo dominant class, which is why molecular diagnosis has a far larger
    counselling and prevention payoff here.
  inheritance_term:
    preferred_term: Autosomal recessive inheritance
    term:
      id: HP:0000007
      label: Autosomal recessive inheritance
  penetrance: COMPLETE
  expressivity: VARIABLE
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24176302
    reference_title: "Genetics of recessive cognitive disorders."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      For autosomal recessive ID (ARID) the recurrence risk is high and, in
      populations with frequent parental consanguinity, ARID is the most common
      form of ID.
    explanation: >-
      States both defining features of this class relative to the dominant
      class: high recurrence risk, and concentration in consanguineous
      populations.
  - reference: PMID:29302074
    reference_title: "Genetics of intellectual disability in consanguineous families."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Autosomal recessive (AR) gene defects are the leading genetic cause of
      intellectual disability (ID) in countries with frequent parental
      consanguinity, which account for about 1/7th of the world population.
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies the population denominator in which autosomal recessive
      inheritance is the dominant mode for intellectual disability.
  - reference: PMID:18452889
    reference_title: "A defect in the TUSC3 gene is associated with autosomal recessive mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      All obligate carriers of this family were heterozygous, but none of 192
      unrelated healthy individuals from the same population carried this
      deletion.
    explanation: >-
      Worked demonstration of the recessive model in a single pedigree:
      unaffected obligate carriers are heterozygous and the allele is absent
      from population controls.
  - reference: PMID:17718851
    reference_title: "Genetics of autosomal recessive non-syndromic mental retardation: recent advances."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      All of the mutations in the ARNSMR-causing genes are protein truncating,
      indicating a putative severe loss-of-function effect.
    explanation: >-
      Characterises the allelic mechanism as biallelic loss of function rather
      than dominant-negative or gain-of-function.
  - reference: PMID:30459488
    reference_title: "Genetics of autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The risk for ARID in children of first cousins or closer is a magnitude
      higher than for children of unrelated parents.
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies the effect of parental relatedness on recessive
      intellectual-disability risk.
- name: Oligogenic / multi-locus inheritance
  description: >-
    A minority of consanguineous families carry pathogenic variants at more than
    one locus, so the phenotype is the sum of two or more recessive lesions
    rather than of a single gene. In the largest systematic look at this, eight
    of 121 large Pakistani families (about 6.6%) segregated multiple pathogenic
    variants across 19 genes. This matters practically: stopping at the first
    convincing homozygous variant can leave part of the phenotype unexplained,
    and recurrence-risk counselling based on a single locus may be wrong.
  inheritance_term:
    preferred_term: Oligogenic inheritance
    term:
      id: HP:0010983
      label: Oligogenic inheritance
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27457812
    reference_title: "Exome sequencing of Pakistani consanguineous families identifies 30 novel candidate genes for recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In another eight families segregation of multiple pathogenic variants was
      observed, affecting 19 genes that were either known or are novel
      candidates for ID.
    explanation: >-
      Direct documentation of multi-locus (oligogenic) causation within a
      consanguineous recessive intellectual-disability cohort.

  measure_type: POINT_PREVALENCE
  prevalence_class: ABOVE_1_IN_1000
  rate_per_100000: 1037.0
  notes: >-
    Prevalence of intellectual disability from all causes, NOT of the autosomal
    recessive non-syndromic subset specifically. AR-NSID is a large but
    unquantified fraction of this denominator; no direct population prevalence
    estimate for the class exists, because ascertainment requires a molecular
    diagnosis that most affected individuals never receive. See the
    `arnsid_no_class_specific_prevalence` discussion.

    supports: SUPPORT

    snippet: >-
      The prevalence of intellectual disability across all 52 studies included
      in the meta-analysis was 10.37/1000 population.
    explanation: >-
      Provides the all-cause intellectual disability denominator from which the
      normalised rate is derived (10.37/1000 = 1037 per 100,000).
  - reference: PMID:28397838
    reference_title: "Mapping autosomal recessive intellectual disability: combined microarray and exome sequencing identifies 26 novel candidate genes in 192 consanguineous families."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Approximately 1% of the global population is affected by intellectual
      disability (ID), and the majority receive no molecular diagnosis.
    explanation: >-
      Independent statement of the same denominator plus the ascertainment
      caveat that prevents a class-specific prevalence figure.
- population: Outbred (non-consanguineous) populations, as a share of affected children
  measure_type: UNKNOWN
  prevalence_class: UNKNOWN
  notes: >-
    Not a population rate but a share of the affected-child cohort: autosomal
    recessive intellectual disability (ARID, syndromic and non-syndromic
    combined) is estimated at about 10% of affected children in an outbred
    population, with an upward tendency as unsolved cases are resolved. Recorded
    as a share rather than a rate because the source expresses it that way;
    the non-syndromic subset is a fraction of this and cannot be separated.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30459488
    reference_title: "Genetics of autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The prevalence of ARID in a cohort of affected children of an outbred
      population is estimated to be about 10%, with an upward tendency in still
      unclarified cases.
    explanation: >-
      The only published quantitative estimate of the recessive share in an
      outbred setting.
- population: Consanguineous populations (Iran, Pakistan, Arabian peninsula and comparable settings)
  measure_type: UNKNOWN
  prevalence_class: COMMON
  notes: >-
    Qualitative class only. In populations with frequent parental consanguinity
    recessive gene defects are the leading genetic cause of intellectual
    disability, and in a highly consanguineous clinical cohort 81% of identified
    point mutations were recessive. No numerator/denominator estimate specific
    to the NON-SYNDROMIC recessive subset has been published; the supporting
    cohorts are clinic-ascertained multiplex families, not population samples.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29302074
    reference_title: "Genetics of intellectual disability in consanguineous families."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Autosomal recessive (AR) gene defects are the leading genetic cause of
      intellectual disability (ID) in countries with frequent parental
      consanguinity, which account for about 1/7th of the world population.
    explanation: >-
      Supports the COMMON qualitative class in the consanguineous stratum.
  - reference: PMID:27431290
    reference_title: "Clinical genomics expands the morbid genome of intellectual disability and offers a high diagnostic yield."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Intellectual disability (ID) is a measurable phenotypic consequence of genetic and
      environmental factors. In this study, we prospectively assessed the diagnostic yield of
      genomic tools (molecular karyotyping, multi-gene panel and exome sequencing) in a cohort of
      337 ID subjects as a first-tier test and compared it with a standard clinical evaluation
      performed in parallel. ... On the other hand, the genomic approach revealed a likely diagnosis
      in 58% (n=196). These included copy number variants in 14% (n=54, 15% are novel), and point
      mutations revealed by multi-gene panel and exome sequencing in the remaining 43% (1% were
      found to have Fragile-X). The identified point mutations were mostly recessive (n=117, 81%),
      consistent with the high consanguinity of the study cohort, but also X-linked (n=8, 6%) and de
      novo dominant (n=19, 13%).
    explanation: >-
      In a selected cohort of 337 individuals with intellectual disability, recessive variants
      comprised 81% of the identified point mutations. This is a diagnostic-yield result in a highly
      consanguineous cohort, not population prevalence of nonsyndromic recessive intellectual
      disability.
  - reference: PMID:24176302
    reference_title: "Genetics of recessive cognitive disorders."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Here we review recent progress in this field, show that ARID is not rare
      even in outbred Western populations, and discuss the prospects for
      improving its diagnosis and prevention.
    explanation: >-
      Important qualifier: the class is not confined to consanguineous
      populations. PARTIAL because the claim is a review conclusion rather than
      a population prevalence survey.

  - preferred_term: PRSS12
    term:
      id: hgnc:9477
      label: PRSS12
  description: >-
    The first AR-NSID gene identified (2002) and the anchor entry of the OMIM
    phenotypic series. Biallelic truncation of PRSS12, encoding the neuronal
    serine protease neurotrypsin, which localises to presynaptic terminals at
    the synaptic cleft. Places the founding member of the class in the
    synaptic-proteolysis theme.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:12459588
    reference_title: "Truncating neurotrypsin mutation in autosomal recessive nonsyndromic mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A 4-base pair deletion in the neuronal serine protease neurotrypsin gene
      was associated with autosomal recessive nonsyndromic mental retardation
      (MR).
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the PRSS12/neurotrypsin subtype and its biallelic truncating
      mechanism.
- name: MRT2
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 2 (CRBN)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 2
    term:
      id: MONDO:0011828
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 2
  genes:
  - preferred_term: CRBN
    term:
      id: hgnc:30185
      label: CRBN
  description: >-
    Homozygous nonsense variant (R419X) in CRBN, encoding cereblon, an
    ATP-dependent Lon protease, in a large North American sectarian kindred.
    Distinctive within the class for its MILD severity band (IQ 50-70) and for
    an explicitly documented absence of dysmorphism, microcephaly, autistic
    features, and neuroimaging abnormality - making it one of the purest
    non-syndromic exemplars. Places protein turnover in the theme set.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:15557513
    reference_title: "A mutation in a novel ATP-dependent Lon protease gene in a kindred with mild mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A nonsense mutation causing a premature stop codon in a novel gene
      (cereblon; CRBN) was identified that encodes for an ATP-dependent Lon
      protease.
    explanation: >-
      Identifies the causal CRBN lesion defining the MRT2 subtype.
  - reference: PMID:15557513
    reference_title: "A mutation in a novel ATP-dependent Lon protease gene in a kindred with mild mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Previously, a disease locus was mapped for a mild type of nonsyndromic
      mental retardation (IQ between 50 and 70) to a 4.2-MB interval on
      chromosome 3p25-pter in a large kindred.
    explanation: >-
      Documents the mild severity band that distinguishes MRT2 from the
      moderate-to-severe presentations typical of the class.
- name: MRT3
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 3 (CC2D1A)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 3
    term:
      id: MONDO:0012037
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 3
  genes:
  - preferred_term: CC2D1A
    term:
      id: hgnc:30237
      label: CC2D1A
  description: >-
    Recurrent protein-truncating founder variant in CC2D1A on 19p13.12,
    identified in nine consanguineous families with SEVERE non-syndromic
    intellectual disability. CC2D1A is a positive regulator of the IKK/NF-kB
    cascade and also restrains PDE4D-dependent cAMP hydrolysis. It is the only
    subtype in this class with a preclinical pharmacological rescue (PDE4
    inhibition in male mice) and is therefore the one druggable-mechanism lead.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:16033914
    reference_title: "The CC2D1A, a member of a new gene family with C2 domains, is involved in autosomal recessive non-syndromic mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A protein truncating mutation was identified in the gene CC2D1A in nine
      consanguineous families with severe autosomal recessive NSMR.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the CC2D1A subtype, its founder truncating allele, and its
      severe phenotype band.
  - reference: PMID:16033914
    reference_title: "The CC2D1A, a member of a new gene family with C2 domains, is involved in autosomal recessive non-syndromic mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      CC2D1A is a putative signal transducer participating in positive
      regulation of I-kappaB kinase/NFkappaB cascade.
    explanation: >-
      Assigns the subtype to the NF-kB signalling theme shared with TRAPPC9.
- name: MRT5
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 5 (NSUN2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 5
    term:
      id: MONDO:0012613
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 5
  genes:
  - preferred_term: NSUN2
    term:
      id: hgnc:25994
      label: NSUN2
  description: >-
    Homozygous loss of the tRNA methyltransferase NSUN2 in Iranian and Kurdish
    consanguineous families, mapping to the previously described MRT5 locus.
    Places RNA (tRNA) modification in the theme set, with a Drosophila
    short-term-memory model providing cross-species functional support. Also the
    clearest example within the class of boundary instability: the authors
    themselves note accompanying facial dysmorphism and raise the possibility
    that the entity is syndromic.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22541559
    reference_title: "Mutations in NSUN2 cause autosomal-recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      that cause a loss of the tRNA-methyltransferase-encoding NSUN2 main
      transcript in homozygotes
    explanation: >-
      Identifies the NSUN2 loss-of-function mechanism defining MRT5.
  - reference: PMID:22541559
    reference_title: "Mutations in NSUN2 cause autosomal-recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      When the Drosophila melanogaster NSUN2 ortholog was deleted, severe
      short-term-memory (STM) deficits were observed; STM could be rescued by
      re-expression of the wild-type protein in the nervous system.
    explanation: >-
      Cross-species functional support that NSUN2 loss impairs memory. PARTIAL
      and MODEL_ORGANISM because the readout is Drosophila short-term memory,
      not the human cognitive phenotype.
- name: MRT6
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 6 (GRIK2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 6
    term:
      id: MONDO:0012614
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 6
  genes:
  - preferred_term: GRIK2
    term:
      id: hgnc:4580
      label: GRIK2
  description: >-
    Complex homozygous rearrangement of GRIK2 (GLUR6), the kainate-type
    ionotropic glutamate receptor subunit, in a large consanguineous Iranian
    family with moderate-to-severe non-syndromic intellectual disability. The
    predicted product lacks the first ligand-binding domain, the adjacent
    transmembrane domain, and the pore loop, giving complete loss of function
    confirmed electrophysiologically. The most direct link in the class between
    the disease and excitatory synaptic transmission.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:17847003
    reference_title: "A defect in the ionotropic glutamate receptor 6 gene (GRIK2) is associated with autosomal recessive mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      cosegregates with moderate-to-severe nonsyndromic autosomal recessive
      mental retardation in a large, consanguineous Iranian family
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the GRIK2 subtype and its moderate-to-severe non-syndromic
      phenotype in a consanguineous pedigree.
  - reference: PMID:17847003
    reference_title: "A defect in the ionotropic glutamate receptor 6 gene (GRIK2) is associated with autosomal recessive mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      The predicted gene product lacks the first ligand-binding domain, the
      adjacent transmembrane domain, and the putative pore loop, suggesting a
      complete loss of function of the GLU(K6) protein, which is supported by
      electrophysiological data.
    explanation: >-
      Functional confirmation of complete loss of receptor function, anchoring
      the synaptic-transmission mechanism.
- name: MRT7
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 7 (TUSC3)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 7
    term:
      id: MONDO:0012615
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 7
  genes:
  - preferred_term: TUSC3
    term:
      id: hgnc:30242
      label: TUSC3
  description: >-
    Homozygous deletion of TUSC3 (N33) on chromosome 8, encoding a subunit of
    the ER-bound oligosaccharyltransferase complex. Mechanistically important
    because it shows a defect in N-glycosylation - a pathway whose other defects
    produce florid multisystem congenital disorders of glycosylation -
    presenting as ISOLATED cognitive impairment, and because it was the first
    gene in the class with mutations reported in more than one family.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:18452889
    reference_title: "A defect in the TUSC3 gene is associated with autosomal recessive mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Haplotype analyses and copy-number studies led to the identification of a
      homozygous deletion partly removing TUSC3 (N33) in all patients.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the biallelic TUSC3 deletion defining MRT7.
  - reference: PMID:18452889
    reference_title: "A defect in the TUSC3 gene is associated with autosomal recessive mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Our data suggest that in contrast to other genetic defects of
      glycosylation, inactivation of TUSC3 causes nonsyndromic MR
    explanation: >-
      Directly supports the non-syndromic designation and contrasts it with the
      syndromic congenital disorders of glycosylation.
- name: MRT13
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 13 (TRAPPC9)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 13
    term:
      id: MONDO:0013173
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 13
  genes:
  - preferred_term: TRAPPC9
    term:
      id: hgnc:30832
      label: TRAPPC9
  description: >-
    Biallelic truncating variants in TRAPPC9 (NIBP) on 8q24, reported
    simultaneously by two groups in 2009 in Pakistani, Iranian, and Israeli Arab
    pedigrees and in many families since. TRAPPC9 is a vesicle-trafficking
    (TRAPP complex) subunit that also activates NF-kB via IKK-beta, converging
    with CC2D1A. It sits at the edge of the non-syndromic definition: variable
    postnatal microcephaly and mild cerebral white matter hypoplasia are common
    but not obligate, and obesity is described in the fuller phenotype. It is
    also the one AR-NSID gene with an established parent-of-origin expression
    bias (see `mechanistic_hypotheses`).
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:20004765
    reference_title: "Identification of mutations in TRAPPC9, which encodes the NIK- and IKK-beta-binding protein, in nonsyndromic autosomal-recessive mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Within this region, we identified a truncating homozygous mutation, R475X,
      in exon 7 of the gene TRAPPC9.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the TRAPPC9 truncating mechanism defining MRT13.
  - reference: PMID:20004765
    reference_title: "Identification of mutations in TRAPPC9, which encodes the NIK- and IKK-beta-binding protein, in nonsyndromic autosomal-recessive mental retardation."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Brain magnetic resonance imaging of affected individuals indicates the
      presence of mild cerebral white matter hypoplasia. Microcephaly is present
      in some but not all affected individuals.
    explanation: >-
      Documents the incompletely penetrant accessory features that make this
      subtype a borderline case for the non-syndromic designation.
  - reference: PMID:20004763
    reference_title: "A truncating mutation of TRAPPC9 is associated with autosomal-recessive intellectual disability and postnatal microcephaly."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      TRAPPC9 is highly expressed in the postmitotic neurons of the cerebral
      cortex, and MRI analysis of affected patients shows defects in axonal
      connectivity.
    explanation: >-
      Independent replication in a separate pedigree, plus the connectivity
      phenotype linking the molecular lesion to cortical circuit formation.
- name: MRT14
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 14 (TECR)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 14
    term:
      id: MONDO:0013528
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 14
  genes:
  - preferred_term: TECR
    term:
      id: hgnc:4551
      label: TECR
  description: >-
    Homozygous missense substitution of a highly conserved proline at codon
    182 of TECR, reported in a consanguineous family whose locus had
    previously been localised to chromosome 19p13. The founding report calls
    the product a synaptic glycoprotein and states that it identified only
    the seventh causal mutation then known for the class, and it uses the
    non-syndromic label throughout. That descriptive phrase is quoted here
    but is NOT used to place the gene: HGNC names hgnc:4551
    trans-2,3-enoyl-CoA reductase, an enzyme name, and this entry carries no
    source establishing a synaptic function for the product, so TECR sits on
    the molecular-function node rather than the synaptic one. Do not read
    synaptic localisation as the mechanism of this subtype.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21212097
    reference_title: "Exome sequencing reveals a novel mutation for autosomal recessive non-syndromic mental retardation in the TECR gene on chromosome 19p13."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      the mutation was homozygous in five affected siblings but in none of
      eight unaffected siblings
    explanation: >-
      Segregation of the homozygous TECR variant with non-syndromic
      intellectual disability in the founding pedigree.
  - reference: PMID:21212097
    reference_title: "Exome sequencing reveals a novel mutation for autosomal recessive non-syndromic mental retardation in the TECR gene on chromosome 19p13."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      This mutation causes a substitution of a leucine for a highly conserved
      proline at amino acid 182 in TECR (trans-2,3-enoyl-CoA reductase), a
      synaptic glycoprotein.
    explanation: >-
      Identifies the causal lesion and the synaptic localisation that places
      this subtype in the synaptic theme.
- name: MRT15
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 15 / Rafiq syndrome (MAN1B1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: Rafiq syndrome
    term:
      id: MONDO:0013624
      label: Rafiq syndrome
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MAN1B1
    term:
      id: hgnc:6823
      label: MAN1B1
  description: >-
    Biallelic variants in MAN1B1 (alpha-1,2-mannosidase) at 9q34.3, a second
    glycosylation entry point alongside TUSC3. Notable as one of the few
    genes in the class with an elevated mutation frequency across
    populations rather than a single-family report. The MONDO label "Rafiq
    syndrome" reflects the subsequent recognition of dysmorphic features in
    some families - within the original report four families were strictly
    non-syndromic while one showed additional clinical features, so this
    subtype straddles the category boundary.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21763484
    reference_title: "Mutations in the alpha 1,2-mannosidase gene, MAN1B1, cause autosomal-recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We have used genome-wide genotyping to identify an overlapping
      homozygosity-by-descent locus on chromosome 9q34.3 (MRT15) in four
      consanguineous families affected by nonsyndromic autosomal-recessive
      intellectual disability (NS-ARID) and one in which the patients show
      additional clinical features.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the MRT15 locus and simultaneously documents the mixed
      syndromic/non-syndromic presentation within the founding cohort.
  - reference: PMID:21763484
    reference_title: "Mutations in the alpha 1,2-mannosidase gene, MAN1B1, cause autosomal-recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      MAN1B1 is one of the few NS-ARID genes with an elevated mutation frequency
      in patients with NS-ARID from different populations.
    explanation: >-
      Supports the claim that this subtype is relatively over-represented in the
      class, unlike the typical single-family genes.
- name: MRT18
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 18 (MED23)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 18
    term:
      id: MONDO:0013651
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 18
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MED23
    term:
      id: hgnc:2372
      label: MED23
  description: >-
    Homozygous missense variant (p.R617Q) in MED23, a subunit of the Mediator
    coactivator complex. Unusually for the class the lesion is a hypomorphic
    missense rather than a truncation, and the demonstrated defect is specific -
    failure of JUN and FOS immediate-early-gene induction rather than global
    transcriptional collapse. Places activity-dependent transcription in the
    theme set.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21868677
    reference_title: "MED23 mutation links intellectual disability to dysregulation of immediate early gene expression."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Here, we report a missense mutation (p. R617Q) in MED23 that cosegregates
      with nonsyndromic autosomal recessive intellectual disability.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the MED23 subtype and its non-syndromic recessive
      cosegregation.
  - reference: PMID:21868677
    reference_title: "MED23 mutation links intellectual disability to dysregulation of immediate early gene expression."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      This mutation specifically impaired the response of JUN and FOS immediate
      early genes (IEGs) to serum mitogens by altering the interaction between
      enhancer-bound transcription factors (TCF4 and ELK1, respectively) and
      Mediator.
    explanation: >-
      Functional mechanism in patient-derived cells: selective loss of
      immediate-early-gene induction, the transcriptional arm of
      activity-dependent plasticity.
- name: MRT27
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 27 (LINS1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 27
    term:
      id: MONDO:0013702
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 27
  genes:
  - preferred_term: LINS1
    term:
      id: hgnc:30922
      label: LINS1
  description: >-
    A homozygous splicing mutation in LINS1 in two sibs of an Emirati family,
    found by homozygosity mapping with whole-exome sequencing and shown by
    transcript analysis to splice exon 4 directly to exon 6. LINS1 is the human
    homologue of the Drosophila segment polarity gene lin and a modulator of WNT
    signalling. WNT signalling is not one of the recurring themes the class
    review names, so this subtype is curated as a loss of a gene-specific
    molecular function without a theme claim. A later Indian family from
    Karnataka with a nonsense variant was reported as non-syndromic intellectual
    disability, and the founding report notes an earlier Iranian family with
    accompanying microcephaly. HGNC records LINS and MRT27 as previous symbols
    for hgnc:30922, so the founding literature calls the gene LINS.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23773660
    reference_title: "LINS, a modulator of the WNT signaling pathway, is involved in human cognition."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Our study confirms that LINS, a modulator of the WNT pathway, is an
      indispensable gene to human cognition
    explanation: >-
      The founding report's own conclusion, establishing LINS1 as a cause of
      recessive cognitive impairment.
  - reference: PMID:23773660
    reference_title: "LINS, a modulator of the WNT signaling pathway, is involved in human cognition."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      LINS is the human homologue of the Drosophila segment polarity gene lin
      that encodes an essential regulator of the wingless/Wnt signaling.
    explanation: >-
      States the gene-specific molecular function whose loss is this subtype's
      mechanism. Graded OTHER because the sentence asserts protein identity
      rather than reporting an experiment.
  - reference: PMID:32499722
    reference_title: "A Novel LINS1 Truncating Mutation in Autosomal Recessive Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Here, we report the clinical characteristics and genetic findings of a
      family with two male siblings affected with autosomal recessive
      nonsyndromic intellectual disability.
    explanation: >-
      An independent family in which the LINS1 phenotype is described as
      non-syndromic, which is what qualifies this subtype for this class.
  - reference: PMID:32499722
    reference_title: "A Novel LINS1 Truncating Mutation in Autosomal Recessive Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      LINS1 has been reported to cause MRT27 (mental retardation, autosomal
      recessive 27), a rare autosomal recessive nonsyndromic intellectual
      disability, with limited characterization of the phenotype.
    explanation: >-
      Names the MRT27 series designation this row is keyed on, and records that
      the phenotype was thinly characterised at the time.

- name: MRT42
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 42 (PGAP1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 42
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014348
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 42
  genes:
  - preferred_term: PGAP1
    term:
      id: hgnc:25712
      label: PGAP1
  description: >-
    Homozygous in-frame deletion in PGAP1, the endoplasmic-reticulum deacylase
    that removes an acyl chain from the inositol of
    glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchors immediately after GPI
    attachment to protein. A third glycosylation entry point into the class
    alongside TUSC3 and MAN1B1, but acting on GPI-anchor remodelling rather
    than N-glycosylation. Mechanistically distinctive because surface levels
    of GPI-anchored proteins were normal in patient cells and only their
    phospholipase sensitivity was lost, so the defect is in anchor STRUCTURE
    rather than in anchor abundance.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24784135
    reference_title: "Null mutation in PGAP1 impairing Gpi-anchor maturation in patients with intellectual disability and encephalopathy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We performed homozygosity mapping and exome sequencing in a family with
      encephalopathy and non-specific ARID and identified a homozygous 3 bp
      deletion (p.Leu197del) in the GPI remodeling gene PGAP1.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the causal PGAP1 lesion and the non-specific (non-syndromic)
      autosomal recessive intellectual-disability presentation.
  - reference: PMID:24784135
    reference_title: "Null mutation in PGAP1 impairing Gpi-anchor maturation in patients with intellectual disability and encephalopathy."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      The expression levels of GPI-APs on B lymphoblastoid cells derived from
      an affected person were normal. However, when those cells were incubated
      with phosphatidylinositol-specific phospholipase C (PI-PLC), GPI-APs
      were cleaved and released from B lymphoblastoid cells from healthy
      individuals whereas GPI-APs on the cells from the affected person were
      totally resistant.
    explanation: >-
      Patient-cell assay showing the defect is in GPI-anchor structure rather
      than in surface abundance of GPI-anchored proteins.
- name: MRT44
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 44 (METTL23)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 44
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014409
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 44
  genes:
  - preferred_term: METTL23
    term:
      id: hgnc:26988
      label: METTL23
  description: >-
    Truncating METTL23 variants in two unrelated families, Austrian and
    Pakistani, both mapped by homozygosity by descent to chromosome 17q25. The
    founding report characterises the phenotype as MILD non-syndromic recessive
    intellectual disability. Both variants truncate the protein, disrupting its
    predicted catalytic domain and altering its cellular localisation; METTL23
    is predicted to be an S-adenosyl-methionine-dependent methyltransferase, and
    its substrate is not established, the founding report naming heat shock
    proteins only as a putative one. METTL23 is already named in this entry's
    molecular-function node as a member of the review's RNA and tRNA
    modification theme, alongside NSUN2, ADAT3 and ELP2. The reported spectrum
    has since widened at the severe end: two sisters homozygous for a frameshift
    variant had severe intellectual disability with facial dysmorphism,
    epilepsy, mitral valve prolapse and, in one, eczema, which their report
    presents as one of the most severe presentations described to date rather
    than as the typical one. The row stays in this class on the entry's
    obligate-feature criterion, and that report's brain imaging was normal, so
    no cortical malformation is in question.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24626631
    reference_title: "Disruption of the methyltransferase-like 23 gene METTL23 causes mild autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We describe the characterization of a gene for mild nonsyndromic
      autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ID) in two unrelated
      families, one from Austria, the other from Pakistan.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the subtype, its two founding families, and the explicitly
      mild and non-syndromic phenotype that places it in this class.
  - reference: PMID:24626631
    reference_title: "Disruption of the methyltransferase-like 23 gene METTL23 causes mild autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      Both changes lead to truncation of the putative METTL23 protein, which
      disrupts the predicted catalytic domain and alters the cellular
      localization.
    explanation: >-
      The molecular consequence of the lesion, measured in the founding report,
      which is this subtype's loss of a gene-specific molecular function.
  - reference: PMID:24626631
    reference_title: "Disruption of the methyltransferase-like 23 gene METTL23 causes mild autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Disruption of METTL23 presented here supports the importance of
      methylation processes for intact neuronal function and brain development.
    explanation: >-
      The authors' placement of the gene in the methylation theme that recurs
      across this class.
  - reference: PMID:42472761
    reference_title: '"Severe intellectual disability with cardiac and dermatologic involvement due to homozygous METTL23 frameshift mutation: a case report of two Turkish sisters".'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Both patients exhibited severe intellectual disability, marked delay in
      speech and self-care, epileptic seizures, and facial dysmorphism
      (depressed nasal bridge, thin upper lip, high hairline, prognathism,
      prominent mandibular angle), along with mitral valve prolapse.
    explanation: >-
      The severe end of the reported spectrum, including the cardiac finding,
      which is why this row records a widened phenotype rather than only the
      founding report's mild one.
  - reference: PMID:42472761
    reference_title: '"Severe intellectual disability with cardiac and dermatologic involvement due to homozygous METTL23 frameshift mutation: a case report of two Turkish sisters".'
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      These cases represent one of the most severe phenotypic presentations of
      METTL23-related intellectual disability reported to date.
    explanation: >-
      The report's own placement of its cases at the severe extreme rather than
      as typical, which is what keeps the obligate-feature criterion satisfied
      and the row inside this class.

- name: MRT45
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 45 (FBXO31)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 45
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014430
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 45
  genes:
  - preferred_term: FBXO31
    term:
      id: hgnc:16510
      label: FBXO31
  description: >-
    Homozygous frameshifting deletion in exon 7 of FBXO31 in a large
    consanguineous Pakistani family, identified by autozygosity mapping plus
    exome and Sanger sequencing, with nonsense-mediated decay contributing
    to loss of the protein. FBXO31 functions as a centrosomal E3 ubiquitin
    ligase in association with SKP1 and Cullin-1, so this subtype is a
    second entry into the regulated-protein-degradation theme alongside
    CRBN. Wired to the cortical-circuit node because the founding report
    attributes FBXO31 roles in neuronal morphogenesis, axonal identity,
    dendrite growth and neuronal migration.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24623383
    reference_title: "Truncation of the E3 ubiquitin ligase component FBXO31 causes non-syndromic autosomal recessive intellectual disability in a Pakistani family."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      This variant leads to a frameshift and a premature stop codon and
      truncation of the FBXO31 protein, p.(Cys283Asnfs*81).
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the truncating FBXO31 lesion defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:24623383
    reference_title: "Truncation of the E3 ubiquitin ligase component FBXO31 causes non-syndromic autosomal recessive intellectual disability in a Pakistani family."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      The FBXO31/SKP1/Cullin1 complex is important for neuronal morphogenesis
      and axonal identity. FBXO31 also plays a role in dendrite growth and
      neuronal migration in developing cerebellar cortex.
    explanation: >-
      The developmental roles the founding report attributes to FBXO31, which
      is why the gene is wired to the cortical-circuit-formation node rather
      than to the synaptic node.
- name: MRT46
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 46 (NDST1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 46
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014499
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 46
  genes:
  - preferred_term: NDST1
    term:
      id: hgnc:7680
      label: NDST1
  description: >-
    Homozygous missense variants in NDST1, a bifunctional GlcNAc
    N-deacetylase/N-sulfotransferase acting in heparan sulfate biosynthesis,
    all reported to date substituting conserved residues of the
    sulfotransferase domain. A heparan sulfate rather than N-glycan entry
    into the glycosylation theme. Sits at the syndromic boundary: across the
    four reported families the founding series describes recurrent muscular
    hypotonia, epilepsy and postnatal growth deficiency alongside the
    intellectual disability, and calls the phenotype distinctive.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25125150
    reference_title: "NDST1 missense mutations in autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Our data confirm NDST1 mutations as a cause of autosomal recessive
      intellectual disability with a distinctive phenotype, and support an
      important function of NDST1 in human development.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes NDST1 as a causal gene for autosomal recessive intellectual
      disability.
  - reference: PMID:25125150
    reference_title: "NDST1 missense mutations in autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Comparing the four families, we noticed significant overlap in the
      clinical features, including both demonstrated and apparent intellectual
      disability, muscular hypotonia, epilepsy, and postnatal growth
      deficiency.
    explanation: >-
      Documents the accessory features that place this subtype at the
      syndromic boundary of the class.
- name: MRT47
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 47 (FMN2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 47
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014524
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 47
  genes:
  - preferred_term: FMN2
    term:
      id: hgnc:14074
      label: FMN2
  description: >-
    Biallelic truncating mutations in FMN2, an actin-cytoskeleton nucleation
    factor of the formin family that is highly expressed in the maturing
    brain, found by homozygosity mapping plus next-generation sequencing in
    two consanguineous families with explicitly non-syndromic disease. The
    mechanism runs through dendritic spine density: FMN2 localises to
    punctae along dendrites, Fmn2-null mice have decreased spine density,
    and patient iPSC-derived neural cells show correspondingly reduced
    synaptic density.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25480035
    reference_title: "Biallelic truncating mutations in FMN2, encoding the actin-regulatory protein Formin 2, cause nonsyndromic autosomal-recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Using a combination of homozygosity mapping and next-generation
      sequencing in two consanguineous families affected by nonsyndromic
      autosomal-recessive intellectual disability, we identified truncating
      mutations in formin 2 (FMN2)
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the FMN2 subtype and its explicitly non-syndromic recessive
      presentation.
  - reference: PMID:25480035
    reference_title: "Biallelic truncating mutations in FMN2, encoding the actin-regulatory protein Formin 2, cause nonsyndromic autosomal-recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      Furthermore, patient neural cells derived from induced pluripotent stem
      cells showed correlated decreased synaptic density.
    explanation: >-
      Patient-derived neuronal evidence for the reduced synaptic density that
      places this subtype on the synaptic-transmission-and-plasticity node.
- name: MRT50
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 50 (EDC3)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 50
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014649
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 50
  genes:
  - preferred_term: EDC3
    term:
      id: hgnc:26114
      label: EDC3
  description: >-
    Homozygous missense variant in EDC3, which stimulates the DCP2 decapping
    enzyme that initiates the 5' to 3' mRNA degradation pathway, reported in
    two affected children of one family. In vitro decapping assays showed
    the altered protein fails to enhance DCP2 decapping at low concentration
    and inhibits it at high concentration. Introduces mRNA decapping into
    the class theme set; the same report identified the 3' to 5' counterpart
    DCPS, whose phenotype is syndromic and therefore modelled separately
    (see notes).
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25701870
    reference_title: "Mutations in DCPS and EDC3 in autosomal recessive intellectual disability indicate a crucial role for mRNA decapping in neurodevelopment."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In another family, we identified a homozygous mutation (c.161T>C;
      p.Phe54Ser) in EDC3 in two affected children.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the causal homozygous EDC3 lesion defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:25701870
    reference_title: "Mutations in DCPS and EDC3 in autosomal recessive intellectual disability indicate a crucial role for mRNA decapping in neurodevelopment."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      In vitro decapping assays showed that altered EDC3 is unable to enhance
      DCP2 decapping at low concentrations and even inhibits DCP2 decapping at
      high concentration.
    explanation: >-
      Functional assay establishing loss of the EDC3 decapping-enhancement
      activity as the molecular defect.
- name: MRT51
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 51 (HNMT)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 51
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014759
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 51
  genes:
  - preferred_term: HNMT
    term:
      id: hgnc:5028
      label: HNMT
  description: >-
    Two homozygous HNMT missense alterations in unrelated consanguineous
    Turkish and Kurdish families with explicitly non-syndromic disease,
    found by autozygosity mapping plus targeted exome sequencing. HNMT
    transfers a methyl group from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to histamine and
    is, per the founding report, the only well-known route for terminating
    histaminergic neurotransmission in the mammalian central nervous system,
    so this subtype places neurotransmitter INACTIVATION on the synaptic
    node - the mirror image of the GRIK2 receptor-loss mechanism. The two
    alleles act by different routes: one abolishes enzymatic activity, the
    other destabilises the protein.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26206890
    reference_title: "Mutations in the histamine N-methyltransferase gene, HNMT, are associated with nonsyndromic autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We performed autozygosity mapping followed by targeted exome sequencing
      and identified two homozygous HNMT alterations, p.Gly60Asp and
      p.Leu208Pro, in patients affected with nonsyndromic autosomal recessive
      intellectual disability from two unrelated consanguineous families of
      Turkish and Kurdish ancestry, respectively.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the HNMT subtype, both founding alleles, and its explicitly
      non-syndromic presentation.
  - reference: PMID:26206890
    reference_title: "Mutations in the histamine N-methyltransferase gene, HNMT, are associated with nonsyndromic autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      Using mutant and wild-type DNA constructs as well as in silico protein
      modeling, we confirmed that p.Gly60Asp disrupts the enzymatic activity
      of the protein, and that p.Leu208Pro results in reduced protein
      stability, resulting in decreased HA inactivation.
    explanation: >-
      Functional demonstration that the two alleles impair histamine
      inactivation by different molecular routes.
- name: MRT52
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 52 (LMAN2L)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 52
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014815
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 52
  genes:
  - preferred_term: LMAN2L
    term:
      id: hgnc:19263
      label: LMAN2L
  description: >-
    A homozygous missense variant in LMAN2L segregating with severe recessive
    intellectual disability and infantile epilepsy in a large consanguineous
    family from Baluchistan, Pakistan, with seven affected individuals.
    LMAN2L encodes an endoplasmic-reticulum cargo receptor for glycoprotein
    transport, so the lesion is loss of a gene-specific molecular function
    rather than entry into a shared pathway. Epilepsy accompanies the
    intellectual disability here; per this entry's boundary criterion epilepsy
    is a non-localising neurological finding rather than a malformation or an
    extra-neural gestalt, which is why this subtype stays in the class
    alongside NDST1, MBOAT7 and KICS2.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26566883
    reference_title: "Homozygous missense mutation in the LMAN2L gene segregates with intellectual disability in a large consanguineous Pakistani family."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      This is the first report linking LMAN2L to a phenotype of severe ARID and
      seizures, indicating that the deleterious homozygous p.R53Q variant very
      likely causes the disorder.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the LMAN2L subtype and the severity and seizure phenotype the
      founding family presented with.
  - reference: PMID:26566883
    reference_title: "Homozygous missense mutation in the LMAN2L gene segregates with intellectual disability in a large consanguineous Pakistani family."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      This homozygous variant was co-segregating in the family with the
      phenotype of severe ID and infantile epilepsy; unaffected family members
      were heterozygous variant carriers.
    explanation: >-
      The recessive segregation that establishes biallelic inheritance, with
      carriers unaffected.
  - reference: PMID:26566883
    reference_title: "Homozygous missense mutation in the LMAN2L gene segregates with intellectual disability in a large consanguineous Pakistani family."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      LMAN2L (OMIM: 609552) encodes for the lectin, mannose-binding 2-like
      protein which is a cargo receptor in the endoplasmic reticulum important
      for glycoprotein transport.
    explanation: >-
      States the gene-specific molecular function whose loss is this subtype's
      mechanism. Graded OTHER because the sentence asserts protein identity
      rather than reporting an experiment.

- name: MRT54
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 54 (TNIK)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 54
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014876
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 54
  genes:
  - preferred_term: TNIK
    term:
      id: hgnc:30765
      label: TNIK
  description: >-
    The same homozygous truncating TNIK mutation, causing complete loss of the
    protein, in two multiplex consanguineous families whose non-syndromic
    intellectual disability maps to a linkage locus on 3q26. TNIK is a kinase
    the founding report credits with an established role in dendrite
    development and synaptic transmission, and the human phenotype is reported
    as consistent with the published Tnik-null mouse. Wired to the synaptic
    node on that basis.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27106596
    reference_title: "A null mutation in TNIK defines a novel locus for intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Exome sequencing of the index in each family revealed the same
      homozygous truncating mutation in TNIK that results in complete loss of
      the protein.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the causal TNIK null lesion shared by both founding
      families.
  - reference: PMID:27106596
    reference_title: "A null mutation in TNIK defines a novel locus for intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      The phenotype we observe in human patients who lack TNIK is consistent
      with the previously published Tnik (-/-) phenotype in the murine model.
    explanation: >-
      Cross-species concordance with the published Tnik-null mouse, cited by
      the founding report as support for causality.
- name: MRT56
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 56 (ZC3H14)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 56
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014930
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 56
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ZC3H14
    term:
      id: hgnc:20509
      label: ZC3H14
  description: >-
    Mutation of ZC3H14, encoding a conserved polyadenosine RNA-binding
    protein, at an intellectual disability locus on chromosome 14q31.3. A
    poly(A)-tail-length rather than a base-modification entry into the
    RNA-metabolism theme. Rodent ZC3H14 protein is expressed in hippocampal
    neurons and colocalises with poly(A) RNA in neuronal cell bodies, and in
    a Drosophila model created by mutating the ortholog dNab2, dNab2 is
    essential for development and required in neurons for normal locomotion
    and flight, with the fly data indicating that it restricts bulk poly(A)
    tail length in vivo.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21734151
    reference_title: "Mutation of the conserved polyadenosine RNA binding protein, ZC3H14/dNab2, impairs neural function in Drosophila and humans."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Here we report a human intellectual disability disease locus on
      chromosome 14q31.3 corresponding to mutation of the ZC3H14 gene that
      encodes a conserved polyadenosine RNA binding protein.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the ZC3H14 subtype, its locus, and the gene product's class.
  - reference: PMID:21734151
    reference_title: "Mutation of the conserved polyadenosine RNA binding protein, ZC3H14/dNab2, impairs neural function in Drosophila and humans."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      Biochemical and genetic data indicate that dNab2 restricts bulk poly(A)
      tail length in vivo, suggesting that this function may underlie its role
      in development and disease.
    explanation: >-
      Molecular function of the ortholog in the Drosophila model, the basis
      for placing this subtype on the molecular-function node.
- name: MRT57
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 57 (MBOAT7)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 57
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014962
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 57
  genes:
  - preferred_term: MBOAT7
    term:
      id: hgnc:15505
      label: MBOAT7
  description: >-
    Homozygous inactivating variants in MBOAT7 (LPIAT1), the acyltransferase
    that loads arachidonic acid onto lysophosphatidylinositol, identified in six
    consanguineous families out of a >5,000-family neurodevelopmental cohort.
    Places membrane phospholipid remodelling in the theme set. Sits at the
    syndromic boundary in the other direction from CRBN: intellectual disability
    is frequently accompanied by epilepsy and autistic features.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27616480
    reference_title: "Mutations in MBOAT7, Encoding Lysophosphatidylinositol Acyltransferase I, Lead to Intellectual Disability Accompanied by Epilepsy and Autistic Features."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      From a cohort of >5,000 families affected by neurodevelopmental disorders,
      we identified six consanguineous families harboring homozygous
      inactivating variants in MBOAT7, encoding lysophosphatidylinositol
      acyltransferase (LPIAT1).
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the MBOAT7 subtype, its biallelic inactivating mechanism, and
      its rarity within a very large neurodevelopmental cohort.
  - reference: PMID:27616480
    reference_title: "Mutations in MBOAT7, Encoding Lysophosphatidylinositol Acyltransferase I, Lead to Intellectual Disability Accompanied by Epilepsy and Autistic Features."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Subjects presented with ID frequently accompanied by epilepsy and autistic features."
    explanation: >-
      Documents the accompanying epilepsy and autistic features that qualify the
      non-syndromic designation for this subtype.

- name: MRT58
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 58 (ELP2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 58
    term:
      id: MONDO:0014996
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 58
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ELP2
    term:
      id: hgnc:18248
      label: ELP2
  description: >-
    Compound heterozygous missense variants in ELP2, a subunit of the
    six-protein Elongator complex that the founding report describes as
    essential to transcription elongation, histone acetylation and tRNA
    modification. ELP2 is already named in the class review's
    tRNA-modification theme alongside NSUN2 and METTL23. Sits at the syndromic
    boundary: the two brothers in the founding report had severe intellectual
    disability with spastic diplegia and self-injury, and clinical information
    about ELP2 variants was described as limited at the time.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25847581
    reference_title: "ELP2 is a novel gene implicated in neurodevelopmental disabilities."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In both brothers, whole exome sequencing revealed a likely pathogenic,
      compound heterozygous missense variant in ELP2.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the biallelic ELP2 lesion defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:25847581
    reference_title: "ELP2 is a novel gene implicated in neurodevelopmental disabilities."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Here we report on two brothers with severe ID, spastic diplegia, and
      self-injury whose presentation eluded a diagnosis for over 20 years.
    explanation: >-
      Documents the accessory motor and behavioural features that place this
      subtype at the syndromic boundary.
- name: MRT59
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 59 (IMPA1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 59
    term:
      id: MONDO:0015020
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 59
  genes:
  - preferred_term: IMPA1
    term:
      id: hgnc:6050
      label: IMPA1
  description: >-
    Homozygous frameshifting 5-bp duplication in IMPA1, cosegregating with
    severe intellectual disability and disruptive behaviour in a large
    consanguineous family from a highly inbred area of northeastern Brazil,
    with the variant genotyped in 26 family members. IMPA1 catalyses the
    final step in the biotransformation of the second messengers inositol
    triphosphate and diacylglycerol, and is the principal target of lithium,
    so this subtype is a second-messenger entry into the class. No clinical
    phenotype had been assigned to IMPA1 dysfunction before this report.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:26416544
    reference_title: "A homozygous loss-of-function mutation in inositol monophosphatase 1 (IMPA1) causes severe intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In a field study performed in a highly inbred area of Northeastern
      Brazil, we identified and investigated a large consanguineous family
      with nine adult members affected by severe ID associated with disruptive
      behavior.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the founding consanguineous pedigree and its severity band
      for this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:26416544
    reference_title: "A homozygous loss-of-function mutation in inositol monophosphatase 1 (IMPA1) causes severe intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      The IMPA1 gene product is responsible for the final step of
      biotransformation of inositol triphosphate and diacylglycerol, two
      second messengers.
    explanation: >-
      The molecular function whose loss defines this subtype's position on the
      molecular-function node.
- name: MRT60
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 60 (TAF13)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 60
    term:
      id: MONDO:0044313
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 60
  genes:
  - preferred_term: TAF13
    term:
      id: hgnc:11546
      label: TAF13
  description: >-
    Two homozygous missense variants in TAF13 in two independent
    consanguineous families, each with two children affected by mild
    intellectual disability and microcephaly. TAF13 and TAF11 form a
    histone-like heterodimer required for their recruitment into the general
    RNA polymerase II transcription factor IID complex, and
    co-immunoprecipitation in transfected cells confirmed that both variants
    impair heterodimer formation. A general-transcription entry into the class
    beside the activity-dependent MED23 mechanism; the severity band is mild.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28257693
    reference_title: "Hypomorphic Pathogenic Variants in TAF13 Are Associated with Autosomal-Recessive Intellectual Disability and Microcephaly."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In two independent consanguineous families each with two children
      affected by mild intellectual disability and microcephaly, we identified
      two homozygous missense variants
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the TAF13 subtype, its two founding families, and its mild
      severity band with microcephaly.
  - reference: PMID:28257693
    reference_title: "Hypomorphic Pathogenic Variants in TAF13 Are Associated with Autosomal-Recessive Intellectual Disability and Microcephaly."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      Co-immunoprecipitation in HeLa cells transfected with plasmids encoding
      TAF11 and TAF13 revealed that both variants indeed impaired formation of
      the TAF13-TAF11 heterodimer, thus confirming the protein modeling
      analysis.
    explanation: >-
      Functional demonstration that the variants disrupt the TFIID-recruitment
      heterodimer, the molecular lesion of this subtype.
- name: MRT61
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 61 (RUSC2)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 61
    term:
      id: MONDO:0030915
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 61
  genes:
  - preferred_term: RUSC2
    term:
      id: hgnc:23625
      label: RUSC2
  description: >-
    Inherited homozygous nonsense mutations in RUSC2, reported for the first
    time in humans in three patients on whole-exome sequencing. RUSC2 codes
    for iporin, a ubiquitous protein with high brain expression that
    interacts with Rab GTPases implicated in intracellular protein
    trafficking, so this subtype is a second vesicle-trafficking entry
    beside TRAPPC9. This is the closest call in the tranche, and the
    criterion in notes item 13 does not settle it cleanly. All three
    patients had central hypotonia and microcephaly as well as moderate to
    severe intellectual disability; microcephaly is not a disqualifier here
    and hypotonia is not a malformation, so those do not move it. Absence of
    the splenium IS a callosal malformation and would disqualify the row if
    it were obligate, but the founding report puts it in two of the three
    patients. It is retained as a subtype on that non-obligate reading, and
    a larger series showing the callosal finding in every case should move
    it to differential_diagnoses.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27612186
    reference_title: "Loss-of-function mutation in RUSC2 causes intellectual disability and secondary microcephaly."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We describe, to our knowledge for the first time, three patients with
      inherited homozygous nonsense mutations identified in RUSC2 on
      whole-exome sequencing.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes RUSC2 as a causal gene and the biallelic nonsense mechanism
      defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:27612186
    reference_title: "Loss-of-function mutation in RUSC2 causes intellectual disability and secondary microcephaly."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      All three patients had central hypotonia, microcephaly, and moderate to
      severe intellectual disability. Two patients had additional features of
      early-onset epilepsy and absence of the splenium.
    explanation: >-
      Documents the accessory features, including a callosal finding, that
      place this subtype at the syndromic boundary of the class.
- name: MRT64
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 64 (LINGO1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 64
    term:
      id: MONDO:0020846
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 64
  genes:
  - preferred_term: LINGO1
    term:
      id: hgnc:21205
      label: LINGO1
  description: >-
    Homozygous missense variants in LINGO1 in two unrelated consanguineous
    families, identified by homozygosity mapping plus exome sequencing and by
    exome sequencing alone, with molecular modelling suggesting both variants
    interfere with glycosylation of the protein. LINGO1 is a
    central-nervous-system transmembrane receptor whose published
    loss-of-function models implicate it in neuronal development and central
    nervous system myelination, which is why it is wired to the
    cortical-circuit node. Sits at the syndromic boundary: all five patients
    had severe intellectual disability with aggressive behaviour and speech
    and motor delay, and four of five were microcephalic.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28837161
    reference_title: "Biallelic variants in LINGO1 are associated with autosomal recessive intellectual disability, microcephaly, speech and motor delay."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We identified homozygous missense variants in LINGO1, p.(Arg290His) in
      family F162 and p.(Tyr288Cys) in family PKMR65.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the two founding LINGO1 alleles defining this subtype.
  - reference: PMID:28837161
    reference_title: "Biallelic variants in LINGO1 are associated with autosomal recessive intellectual disability, microcephaly, speech and motor delay."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      Published loss-of-function studies in mouse and zebrafish have
      established a crucial role of LINGO1 in normal neuronal development and
      central nervous system myelination by negatively regulating
      oligodendrocyte differentiation and neuronal survival.
    explanation: >-
      The developmental role the founding report cites from prior animal
      models, the basis for wiring LINGO1 to the cortical-circuit-formation
      node.
- name: MRT66
  display_name: Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 66 (FERRY3, formerly C12orf4)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 66
    term:
      id: MONDO:0032605
      label: intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 66
  genes:
  - preferred_term: FERRY3
    term:
      id: hgnc:1184
      label: C12orf4
  description: >-
    A founder missense variant in seven affected individuals from two Finnish
    consanguineous families plus a deletion in one affected individual from a
    consanguineous Dutch family, with both variants cosegregating as an
    autosomal recessive trait. Phenotype is mild to moderate intellectual
    disability with neuropsychiatric symptoms and delayed speech development.
    Unusual within the class for a measured population carrier frequency: the
    Finnish founder allele reaches 1:53 among blood donors in the North
    Eastern sub-isolate of Finland, so this is one of the few MRT subtypes
    with a quantified regional carrier burden rather than a single-family
    report.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27311568
    reference_title: "Identification of C12orf4 as a gene for autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Our findings implicate C12orf4 as a causative gene for autosomal
      recessive ID.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the gene now approved as FERRY3 as causal for autosomal
      recessive intellectual disability.
  - reference: PMID:27311568
    reference_title: "Identification of C12orf4 as a gene for autosomal recessive intellectual disability."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Screening of the p.Leu328Pro variant showed enrichment in the North
      Eastern sub-isolate of Finland among anonymous local blood donors with a
      carrier frequency of 1:53
    explanation: >-
      Quantifies the Finnish founder-allele carrier frequency, unusual for a
      subtype in this class.
- name: MRT68
  display_name: Intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal recessive 68 (TRMT1)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal recessive 68
    term:
      id: MONDO:0032665
      label: intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal recessive 68
  genes:
  - preferred_term: TRMT1
    term:
      id: hgnc:25980
      label: TRMT1
  description: >-
    Biallelic TRMT1 variants, now reported in a cohort of 43 individuals from 31
    unrelated families, in whom developmental delay and intellectual disability
    are universal while behavioural abnormalities, epilepsy and facial
    dysmorphism are variable. TRMT1 is a tRNA methyltransferase that
    dimethylates a single guanine at position 26 of most tRNAs, which puts this
    subtype on the same molecular-function node as the RNA and tRNA modification
    genes already recorded there: NSUN2, ADAT3, ELP2 and METTL23. The theme list
    this entry transcribes from the class review does not itself name TRMT1, so
    the placement is this entry's rather than the review's. Cells from affected
    individuals are deficient in the tRNA modifications TRMT1 catalyses, which
    ties the clinical entity to the molecular lesion. Sits inside the class
    rather than at its boundary on the strength of that variability: the
    accompanying features are explicitly not obligate, so the entity is
    recognised by its cognitive phenotype plus its molecular lesion.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40245862
    reference_title: "Bi-allelic pathogenic variants in TRMT1 disrupt tRNA modification and induce a neurodevelopmental disorder."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Here, we describe a comprehensive cohort of 43 individuals from 31
      unrelated families with bi-allelic variants in tRNA methyltransferase 1
      (TRMT1).
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the subtype on a cohort large enough to characterise which of
      its features are obligate.
  - reference: PMID:40245862
    reference_title: "Bi-allelic pathogenic variants in TRMT1 disrupt tRNA modification and induce a neurodevelopmental disorder."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      These individuals present with a neurodevelopmental disorder universally
      characterized by developmental delay and intellectual disability,
      accompanied by variable behavioral abnormalities, epilepsy, and facial
      dysmorphism.
    explanation: >-
      The sentence the subtype-versus-differential call turns on: cognition is
      affected universally while the accompanying features, dysmorphism
      included, are variable rather than obligate.
  - reference: PMID:40245862
    reference_title: "Bi-allelic pathogenic variants in TRMT1 disrupt tRNA modification and induce a neurodevelopmental disorder."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      Moreover, cells derived from individuals harboring TRMT1 variants exhibit
      a deficiency in tRNA modifications catalyzed by TRMT1.
    explanation: >-
      Demonstrates in patient-derived cells the loss of the gene-specific
      molecular function this subtype is wired to.
  - reference: PMID:26308914
    reference_title: "The Role of a Novel TRMT1 Gene Mutation and Rare GRM1 Gene Defect in Intellectual Disability in Two Azeri Families."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In the first family, a missense variant was found in GRM1 gene, while in
      the second family, a frameshift alteration was identified in TRMT1, both
      of which were found to co-segregate with the disease.
    explanation: >-
      The founding consanguineous family, identified by autozygosity mapping
      with exome sequencing, that first supported TRMT1 as a recessive
      intellectual-disability gene.
  - reference: PMID:26308914
    reference_title: "The Role of a Novel TRMT1 Gene Mutation and Rare GRM1 Gene Defect in Intellectual Disability in Two Azeri Families."
    supports: SUPPORT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      the TRMT1 gene encodes a tRNA methyltransferase that dimethylates a single
      guanine residue at position 26 of most tRNAs using S-adenosyl methionine
      as the methyl group donor
    explanation: >-
      States the gene-specific molecular function whose loss is this subtype's
      mechanism. Graded OTHER because the sentence asserts enzyme identity
      rather than reporting an experiment.

- name: MRT69
  display_name: Intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal recessive 69 (ZBTB11)
  classification: molecular
  subtype_term:
    preferred_term: intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal recessive 69
    term:
      id: MONDO:0032715
      label: intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal recessive 69
  genes:
  - preferred_term: ZBTB11
    term:
      id: hgnc:16740
      label: ZBTB11
  description: >-
    Two families segregating biallelic ZBTB11 missense variants predicted to
